headword: {体調|たいちょう}を{崩|くず}す
gloss: to fall ill; to get out of shape health-wise

definitions.gloss: to fall ill; to lose one's health; to become unwell
definitions.explanation: To have one's physical condition deteriorate, typically due to overwork, stress, lack of sleep, seasonal changes, or other factors. Implies a decline from a previously healthy state.

examples.japanese: {体調|たいちょう}を{崩|くず}した。
{季節|きせつ}の{変|か}わり{目|め}に{体調|たいちょう}を{崩|くず}しやすい。
examples.english: It's easy to get sick at the change of seasons.

examples.japanese: {無理|むり}をしすぎて{体調|たいちょう}を{崩|くず}し、{一週間|いっしゅうかん}{会社|かいしゃ}を{休|やす}んだ。
examples.english: I pushed myself too hard, fell ill, and took a week off from work.

notes:
USAGE:
A very common and natural way to express becoming unwell in Japanese. More neutral and everyday than {病気|びょうき}になる (to get sick), which implies a specific illness. {体調|たいちょう}を{崩|くず}す covers a broader range of health decline, from mild fatigue to serious illness.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {体調|たいちょう}を{崩|くず}しやすい (prone to falling ill)
- {体調|たいちょう}を{崩|くず}して{休|やす}む (to take time off due to illness)
- {無理|むり}をして{体調|たいちょう}を{崩|くず}す (to fall ill from overexertion)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {病気|びょうき}になる: to get sick — implies a specific, diagnosable illness
- {具合|ぐあい}が{悪|わる}い: to feel unwell — describes the current state rather than the change
